t.2.43.1: Rāma too, that tiger among men, mindful of his father's command, travelled a great distance in that very remainder of the night.
t.2.43.2: As he went on in this way, the auspicious night passed away; having performed the auspicious twilight worship, he entered the border of the realm.
t.2.43.3: Gazing at those villages with fields ploughed out to their boundaries, and at the flowering woods, he swiftly passed beyond them, borne by his finest horses as if by arrows.
t.2.43.4: He heard the words of the people dwelling in the village settlements: "Shame on King Daśaratha, who has come under the sway of desire!"
t.2.43.5: Alas, today the cruel Kaikeyī, wicked and bent on wickedness, harsh and having broken all bounds of propriety, is engaged in a harsh deed.
t.2.43.6: She who sends into exile, to dwell in the forest, such a son of the king, righteous, supremely wise, compassionate and tireless.
t.2.43.7: Hearing these words of the people who dwelt in the villages and settlements, the heroic lord of Kosala passed beyond the land of the Kosalas.
t.2.43.8: Then, having crossed the river named Vedaśruti, which carries auspicious waters, he went on, facing toward the quarter inhabited by Agastya.
t.2.43.9: Having travelled for a very long time, he then crossed the river Gomatī, cool of water and flowing to the sea, whose marshy banks were thronged with cattle.
t.2.43.10: Having crossed the Gomatī as well, Rāghava, with his swift horses, crossed the river Syandikā, resounding with the cries of peacocks and swans.
t.2.43.11: Rāma showed Vaidehī the prosperous land, filled with realms, which King Manu had given to Ikṣvāku of old.
t.2.43.12: Addressing that charioteer again and again with the word "Sūta!", the glorious bull among men, whose voice was like that of an impassioned swan, spoke.
t.2.43.13: When shall I return once more and go roaming on the hunt in the flowering forest by the Sarayū, united again with my mother and father?
t.2.43.14: I do not greatly long for hunting in the forest by the Sarayū, though this is indeed a delight unequalled in the world, esteemed by hosts of royal seers.
t.2.43.15: The descendant of Ikṣvāku travelled along that road, speaking to the charioteer in a sweet voice and turning his words to one matter after another.
